answer:
**Selection can manufacture a negative relationship between independent skills.** Let coding and research each be independently strong with probability one half. The four combinations—neither, coding only, research only, both—each occur one quarter of the time. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

Interview anyone strong in at least one skill. The “neither” group disappears, leaving three equally common combinations. Among interviewed applicants without coding strength, everyone must have research strength. Among those with coding strength, only half also have research strength.

**Calculate the induced association.** In the selected sample, each skill has mean two thirds and their product has mean one third. Covariance is $1/3-(2/3)^2=-1/9$. In the original population it was zero.

Nothing in the example says coding reduces research ability. The interview indicator is a collider, and conditioning on it creates the association. A model trained only on interviewees may therefore learn relationships that do not generalize to all applicants. Understand the selection mechanism and target population before interpreting the correlation or collecting more of the same selected data.

**Technical details and references.**

Let coding strength $C$ and research strength $R$ be independent Bernoulli(0.5), and interview an applicant when $I=C\lor R$. The population has four equally likely skill combinations; among interviewees, (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1) each have probability one third. Therefore $P(R=1|C=0,I=1)=1$, but $P(R=1|C=1,I=1)=1/2$. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

The conditional covariance is $1/3-(2/3)(2/3)=-1/9$: an apparent negative association produced entirely by selection on the collider $I$. It does not show that coding reduces research skill. A model trained only on interviewed applicants inherits this selected population and may generalize poorly to all candidates. Use the selection mechanism and intended population to guide data collection and evaluation rather than interpreting the observed correlation causally.
